name: Cyclone Plateau
geological_features: Stable atmospheric plateaus where pressure creates flat cloud layers
Permanent cyclonic storms anchored to the plateaus
Metallic hydrogen ocean beneath the cloud deck
Ammonia crystal formations in the upper atmosphere
specific_features: Atmospheric microbes that form visible colonial structures within the cloud plateaus
description: Cyclone Plateau is an enormous gas giant whose most distinctive feature is a series of stable atmospheric pressure zones that create flat, plateau-like cloud formations. These plateaus persist for centuries, anchoring permanent cyclonic storms that rotate with mechanical regularity. Below the visible cloud deck, a sea of metallic hydrogen extends to the planet's crushing core.

The upper atmosphere is a canvas of amber, rust, and cream, with the cyclone systems painting spiral patterns visible from millions of kilometers away. Lightning arcs between cloud layers in continuous cascades, illuminating the depths in stroboscopic flashes. The scale is humbling: a single cyclone system could swallow a terrestrial world whole.

Atmospheric microbes inhabit the cloud plateaus, forming colonial structures large enough to be detected by orbital sensors. These organisms float in the narrow pressure band where temperatures and chemistry permit life, rising and falling with atmospheric currents. Their existence suggests that life in gas giant atmospheres may be far more common than previously assumed.

Cyclone Plateau's helium-3 and fusion fuel reserves are of enormous strategic value, and several orbital harvesting stations skim the upper atmosphere. The discovery of atmospheric life has complicated extraction operations, as regulations now require harvesting corridors to avoid known colonial concentrations. The antimatter traces detected in the deepest atmospheric layers remain tantalizingly out of reach.
